title: Choosing and shelving fresh produce
target: How to handle the fresh side of a Supermarket Simulator shop, given that each fruit and vegetable is its own named good, that the produce stall places goods for you, and that weighing is a routine on the scale.
prerequisites: A produce stall or the space for one
A scale with a barcode to scan
Room in the chiller for what you buy

steps.do: Buy fresh goods as individual lines rather than as one lump of stock.
steps.because: each fresh good is shipped with a picture of its own, an artichoke, an avocado, a banana and a carrot among them (Artichoke, Avocado, Banana, Carrot)

steps.do: Set them out on the produce stall and let the stall space them.
steps.because: the produce stall has a calculator of its own for where a product goes (ProduceStallProductTransformCalculator)

steps.do: Take anything sold by weight to the scale, not to the shelf.
steps.because: the scale is a system of its own with a manager, a controller and its own data (ScaleManager, Scale, ScaleController, ScaleData)

steps.do: Scan the barcode or key in the code when the scale asks for it.
steps.because: both ways of identifying a weighed good are provided (Barcode, ScaleApplyBarcodeTask, ScaleEnterCodeTask)

steps.do: Wait for the customer the scale is weighing for rather than walking away.
steps.because: the scale has a step where it waits for the customer (ScaleWaitCustomerTask)

steps.do: Keep the tinned goods in their own lines beside the fresh ones.
steps.because: tinned goods are named per brand and per kind, green beans, cayenne pepper, crushed pineapple, mixed fruit, tomato and corn among them (253_Canned_Beaneto_GreenBeans, 260_Canned_RedRock_Tomato, 262_Canned_SunValley_Corn)

commonMistakes: Putting fresh goods on an ordinary shelf slot and wondering why they do not sit right.
Walking off while the scale is still waiting on a customer.
Mixing tinned lines together so that two brands share one space.
Buying produce before checking what the scale needs for it.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
